The test image shows two tomato stems cut longitudinally, revealing internal vascular browning/discoloration. The outer stem is mostly green but with tan/brown streaking, and the roots are fibrous and brown. This pattern strongly suggests a vascular wilt disease.

Top candidates: Verticillium_Wilt, Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato.

Let me view reference images from 8 different classes.

I've now viewed 8 reference images from 8 different classes. Let me summarize my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Two tomato stems (with root systems) laid on white background, split/cut longitudinally
- Significant brown/tan vascular and pith discoloration throughout the internal stem tissue
- External stem surface mostly green with some browning
- Brown fibrous roots showing damage
- No white mycelium, no sclerotia, no leaf lesions visible

**Reference comparison:**
- **Bacterial_Wilt/Bugwood_3**: Stem cross-section with brown vascular discoloration + bacterial streaming — similar internal browning pattern but streaming not shown in test
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt/Bugwood_5**: Wilted plants with tan/white stems and root systems exposed — most similar overall presentation
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Showed leaf V-lesions and whole-plant yellowing — doesn't match stem-section view
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Whole-plant wilt in field — doesn't match
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Streaming test — doesn't match the dried internal tissue pattern

The brown internal vascular/pith discoloration visible in the longitudinal stem sections, combined with the fibrous brown roots, most closely matches **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato**, which causes characteristic internal brown streaking and pith necrosis visible in cut stems.
